# #4120: Patch: follow-up to #4098 from the after-merge spot-check
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

<!-- jackioh-bot:spot-check-follow-up #4098 -->
The after-merge spot-check of #4098 ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44056054410)) found 1 blocking problem(s) in the change as it merged (`a5d9d4864f12`). `claude-3` (claude, `opus`, strong) reviewed it. #4098 stays merged: nothing is reverted, and this issue fixes what it found in a change of its own, from `main`.

## What to fix

- [ ] `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs:5677`: `a_corpus_record_uses_its_pinned_endings_channel_flag` requires seed 3760's channel game to end by concede, accepted draw, disconnect or match ceiling. That is a chance outcome of one drifting game, not a property of the change, so unrelated card, engine or AI changes will turn this per-PR test red.
  Evidence: The test is not `#[ignore]`d, so it runs in the per-PR `tools fuzz` group (`.github/ci/rust-test.toml`: `-p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh -- fuzz:: ...`). `scripts/ci-scope.sh` turns that group on for card and engine changes. A channel game ends early only with `ENDINGS_END_CHANCE` = 0.004 per step. Over the ~100–130 actions of seed 3760's game that is roughly a 35–40% chance, so whenever a change to any of its 50 pinned cards, the engine or the policy alters the game, `assert!(ENDINGS_TERMINAL_REASONS.contains(&with.reason...))` most likely fails. The `assert_ne!(with.hash, without.hash)` that follows already proves `replay_record` uses `record.endings`. The plan asked for something sturdier: check that the log holds an action the policy never sends (via `play_game_with_options`). Fix: drop the terminal-reason assertion, or replace it with that log check. The `!ENDINGS_TERMINAL_REASONS.contains(&without.reason)` half is also always true: `check_termination` already refuses those reasons when there is no channel.

## Done when

- Each finding above is fixed where it points, or answered with the evidence that it does not hold.
- Every check is green, with no test skipped, ignored or weakened to get there (CLAUDE.md rule 12).

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44057423579)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Fix the flaky per-PR test `a_corpus_record_uses_its_pinned_endings_channel_flag` so it asserts a property of the change instead of a chance outcome of seed 3760's drifting game. Done when both `ENDINGS_TERMINAL_REASONS` assertions are gone, the remaining `assert_ne!(with.hash, without.hash)` still proves `replay_record` honors `record.endings`, and every check below is green with nothing skipped or weakened.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes there |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs` | change | `fuzz::tests::fuzz_regression_corpus::a_corpus_record_uses_its_pinned_endings_channel_flag` (lines ~5675–5685): delete both terminal-reason assertions, keep the hash assertion, add a why-comment |

Do not touch `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/*.json`, or anything under `spec/`. No new ruling note and no spec change: this is a test-only fix, not a rules decision the spec leaves open (CLAUDE.md rule 3 does not trigger). Governing spec sections, for context only: §2.5 (how games end; R79, R84), §9.3 (`(seed, log)` reconstructs the match), §10.7 (the policy and `AI_SKIPPED_ACTIONS`).

## Steps

1. In `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`, re-read `a_corpus_record_uses_its_pinned_endings_channel_flag` (in `mod fuzz_regression_corpus`, ~line 5659) and confirm it contains the two assertions on `ENDINGS_TERMINAL_REASONS` followed by `assert_ne!(with.hash, without.hash, "replay_record ignored record.endings")`. Confirm `ENDINGS_TERMINAL_REASONS` (line ~903) is still referenced by `check_termination` (~line 1445), so deleting the test's uses removes nothing the gate needs.
2. Delete exactly these two assertions and nothing else:
```rust
            assert!(
                ENDINGS_TERMINAL_REASONS.contains(&with.reason.as_str()),
                "seed 3760's pinned channel ended by {}",
                with.reason
            );
            assert!(
                !ENDINGS_TERMINAL_REASONS.contains(&without.reason.as_str()),
                "seed 3760 without the channel ended by {}",
                without.reason
            );
```
Copy the pattern from the sibling test `a_corpus_record_uses_its_pinned_dealt_seats` in the same module, which proves its flag the same sturdy way: replay both variants and assert the hashes differ, with no assertion on the stochastic game outcome.
3. Directly above the surviving `assert_ne!(with.hash, without.hash, "replay_record ignored record.endings");` line, insert this comment and keep the assertion byte-identical:
```rust
            // No assertion on the terminal reason: whether this seed's channel game ends
            // through the channel is chance (ENDINGS_END_CHANCE per step), so any
            // game-altering card, engine or policy change can flip it; the second
            // half was vacuous besides (check_termination already refuses those
            // reasons without the channel). The hash comparison below is the
            // property of the change: it proves replay_record uses record.endings.
```
4. Run `cargo fmt --check`, then `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh fuzz_regression_corpus`, then `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`. All three must pass; fix honestly if they do not (no `#[ignore]`, no deleted or emptied test, no new `#[allow(...)]`).

## Tests

- Updated test, in `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`, `fuzz::tests::fuzz_regression_corpus::a_corpus_record_uses_its_pinned_endings_channel_flag`: reads the corpus, finds seed 3760, replays it with `endings: true` and with `endings: false` via `replay_record` (both must succeed, as today), and asserts the two hashes differ. It no longer asserts anything about either run's terminal reason.
- No new test is added: the fix deletes flaky assertions, and the surviving hash assertion in the same test is the coverage. The rejected alternative (assert the log holds a channel-only action such as `Concede` via `play_game_with_options`) was deliberately not chosen: `Passed` carries no log, so it needs new plumbing for the same residual chance at higher implementation risk, and the issue permits the deletion.
- Commands (run in this order, all must pass):
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh a_corpus_record_uses_its_pinned_endings_channel_flag`
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh fuzz_regression_corpus` (module sweep for siblings)
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`

## Done when

- [ ] Both `ENDINGS_TERMINAL_REASONS` assertions are gone from `a_corpus_record_uses_its_pinned_endings_channel_flag`; the hash assertion and the why-comment are in their place.
- [ ] The `!ENDINGS_TERMINAL_REASONS.contains(&without.reason...)` half is gone with it (it could never fail per `check_termination`).
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh fuzz_regression_corpus` passes, with no test ignored, skipped, or weakened.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.
- [ ] No file outside `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs` changed; no ruling note added or removed.

## Risks

- Residual chance in the surviving hash assertion: if a future game change makes seed 3760's channel send no action at all (roughly a 1–3% event per game-altering change at `ENDINGS_END_CHANCE` 0.004 plus `ENDINGS_ACT_CHANCE` 0.03 over ~100–130 actions), the two hashes would coincide and the test would fail. Accepted because the issue explicitly blesses this assertion as the proof, and it replaces a ~60% flake with a ~1–3% one; the fully deterministic variant (unit-testing `endings_action` wiring directly) is out of scope for this issue.
- `with.reason` / `without.reason` become unread after the deletion; that is intended. `ENDINGS_TERMINAL_REASONS` stays live through `check_termination`, so no dead-code lint follows.
- Replay determinism: `replay_record` replays pinned decks plus the pinned `endings` flag through fixed `Rng` streams, so both replays are exact on any machine; the change alters no stream and no game code.

## Open questions

None.

## Tests

- Updated test, in `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`, `fuzz::tests::fuzz_regression_corpus::a_corpus_record_uses_its_pinned_endings_channel_flag`: reads the corpus, finds seed 3760, replays it with `endings: true` and with `endings: false` via `replay_record` (both must succeed, as today), and asserts the two hashes differ. ## Risks

- Residual chance in the surviving hash assertion: if a future game change makes seed 3760's channel send no action at all (roughly a 1–3% event per game-altering change at `ENDINGS_END_CHANCE` 0.004 plus `ENDINGS_ACT_CHANCE` 0.03 over ~100–130 actions), the two hashes would coincide and the test would fail. Accepted because the issue explicitly blesses this assertion as the proof, and it replaces a ~60% flake with a ~1–3% one; the fully deterministic variant (unit-testing `endings_action` wiring directly) is out of scope for this issue.
- `with.reason` / `without.reason` become unread after the deletion; that is intended. `ENDINGS_TERMINAL_REASONS` stays live through `check_termination`, so no dead-code lint follows.
- Replay determinism: `replay_record` replays pinned decks plus the pinned `endings` flag through fixed `Rng` streams, so both replays are exact on any machine; the change alters no stream and no game code.
